target_customer: Developers and companies embedding document viewing and annotation into web and mobile apps; also individuals marking up PDFs
problem: Viewing Office and PDF files in a browser required Flash plugins or downloads. Crocodoc converted documents to HTML5 for viewing, commenting and embedding.
business_model: Usage-based API and premium features for document viewing
product_category: HTML5 document viewer and annotation API

founders.name: Ryan Damico
founders.background_notes: YC page lists later roles at Box, Wayfair, Meta and Stripe; he became Box director of platform after the acquisition.

founders.name: Matt Long
founders.background_notes: YC page: built the infrastructure and document conversion API.

founders.name: Bennett Rogers
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no bio.

competitors.name: Scribd
competitors.what: Document sharing site with iPaper Flash embeds, HTML5 reader for its own site
competitors.traction_then: Over 20 million embeds upgraded to HTML5 in March 2011

competitors.name: Google Docs viewer
competitors.what: Embeddable document viewer with imperfect formatting

technical_complexity.rationale: High fidelity conversion of Office and PDF files into HTML5 and CSS3 at scale was hard in 2010 and 2011, and the infrastructure was built by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Conversion quality and speed were hard to replicate quickly, but large players like Scribd and Google could also build it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Scribd upgraded embeds to HTML5 in March 2011. Box bought the company in May 2013 with its seven person team.

market_need_then: Flash based viewers failed on iPads and phones, and customers including Dropbox, Yammer and LinkedIn used Crocodoc to render documents; users uploaded millions of documents monthly per the YC page.

branding.domain_note: crocodoc.com; crocodoc.com did not resolve in this session. Domain history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable playful name, but no source covers logo, mascot or brand press; growth came through developer and enterprise customers.

pivots.to: Embeddable HTML5 document viewer with API
pivots.why: Relaunched in February 2011 for embedding and developers; earlier 2010 focus was team collaboration on PDFs per TechCrunch.

outcome_analysis: Crocodoc started as a web PDF markup tool, raised an undisclosed angel round in July 2010 from Dave McClure, Joshua Schachter, Paul Buchheit and others and relaunched in February 2011 as an HTML5 viewer with an API. It won enterprise developer customers and Box acquired it on 9 May 2013 for an undisclosed mix of cash and stock, taking in its seven person team. The mobile shift away from Flash and strong conversion technology explain the exit.
notes: The YC page says the company was founded in 2007 while CB Insights and Seedtable say 2010; MIT News describes it as an offshoot of WebNotes. CB Insights total of 20K dollars looks wrong and is ignored. Competitor entries come from search result summaries of the 2009 and 2011 TechCrunch pieces, not full reads. Peter Lai's listing as founder is from the YC page and not confirmed by launch press.
